newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 1996/97 coffee output seen up 15.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 1996/97 coffee output seen up 15.7 pct.

text.p: Philippine coffee production is seen rising by 15.7 percent to 59,000 tonnes for the crop year July 1996 to June 1997, the Philippines' International Coffee Organization Certifying Agency (Icoca) said on Friday.
Icoca executive director Antonio Reyes told Reuters that of the 59,000 tonnes estimated production, 48,600 will be consumed by the domestic market.
The remaining 10,400 tonnes will be exported. In crop year 1995/1996 (July-June), the country's coffee production was at 51,000 of which 2,400 tonnes were exported.

Reyes said Philippine exports for the coffee year 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) totalled 1,382 tonnes, a 62.9 percent drop from 3,722 tonnes the previous coffee year. Value of the exports plummeted by 63.9 percent to $4.11 million from the previous $11.37 million.
Reyes said the drop in export value was a result of falling prices of green coffee beans in the world market.
He said local traders preferred to sell to the domestic market where the average per kilogram coffee is three pesos higher than world prices.
